senses.sense_definition: A thin, narrow strip of wood or metal fastened to building frames to support plaster, tiles, or other coverings.

examples.text: The workers nailed each wooden <w>lath</w> horizontally across the ceiling frame before applying plaster.
Renovating the historic home revealed layers of old <w>lath</w> and plaster behind the wallpaper.

senses.sense_definition: A thick, sharp-edged plank driven forward to hold back loose soil or mud during tunneling or excavation.

examples.text: Engineers drove a heavy steel <w>lath</w> forward to stabilize the loose soil above the tunnel.
Each protective <w>lath</w> was hammered into place to keep mud from spilling into the pit.

senses.sense_definition: A microscopic, needle-shaped crystal, commonly of plagioclase feldspar, embedded in a glassy groundmass.

examples.text: Under the microscope, the geologist identified a tiny mineral <w>lath</w> inside the volcanic rock specimen.
Each plagioclase <w>lath</w> was surrounded by a fine-grained, glassy matrix in the basalt sample.

senses.sense_definition: Alternative form of <w>lat</w> (a staff or monumental pillar).

examples.text: The ancient stone <w>lath</w> stood prominently at the entrance of the temple complex.
Scholars documented the royal inscriptions carved into the monumental <w>lath</w> erected centuries ago.

senses.sense_definition: To cover or line a surface with laths.

examples.text: Carpenters will <w>lath</w> the interior walls before the plasterers arrive next week.
They carefully <w>lathed</w> the wooden framework of the old cottage during the restoration.
